newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn urges quick Airbus restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Bonn urges quick Airbus restructuring.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Monday urged the European partners in the Airbus consortium to move quickly to adapt a new structure to meet the challenge from a merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.

"Airbus Industrie and its partners must agree as soon as possible on an optimal structure that will allow Airbus Industrie to match its American competitors as a powerful, integrated European enterprise," he said in a statement.

Rexrodt added that Europe's aerospace industry could not remain idle in the face of Boeing's "monopoly on aircraft with more than 400 seats (B747-Jumbo)" and indicated that European political support should be given to the Airbus consortium.
He noted that the Bonn government has actively supported the Airbus consortium since its inception 25 years ago.
"In this business which is strongly affected by state influence the German government will make its contribution in future to ensure fair competition on the world market," he said in a statement.

Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, the world's first and third-largest aircraft makers, at the weekend announced plans to merge and form the world's biggest aerospace company with annual sales of $48 billion and employ 200,000 employees. The merger is valued at $13.3 billion with a stock swap. It must still be approved by U.S. authorities.
Since the planned merger was announced, European attention has focused on the slow-moving talks within the Airbus consortium to create a single integrated European aerospace company by 1999.
"If we could reach this goal before 1999 that would be good," said Theodor Benien, a spokesman for Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), the German Airbus partner.
Benien added that the Airbus consortium remained committed to building a jumbo carrier for civilian air transport, but that it was still searching for global partners to finance the project.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, DASA, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
